title: Bisimplicial span induced by maps of special resolutions
statement: Use the model-category axioms and Reedy structures of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] and weak homotopy equivalences of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Let $\mathcal M,\mathcal N$ be model categories, $T:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ a functor, $S:\Delta\to\mathcal M$ and $B:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal M$ diagrams, and $S':\Delta\to\mathcal N$, $B':\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal N$ diagrams. Suppose $a:TS\to S'$ and $b:TB\to B'$ are natural transformations. Suppose every component of $a$ is a weak equivalence between cofibrant objects, and $B'$ is Reedy fibrant and homotopically constant (all its structure maps are weak equivalences). Set $D_{m,n}=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(S^m,B_n)$, $E_{m,n}=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal N}(TS^m,B'_n)$ and $D'_{m,n}=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal N}(S'^m,B'_n)$. The formulas $h\mapsto b_nT(h)$ and $h'\mapsto h'a^m$ define maps of bisimplicial sets $D\to E\leftarrow D'$, and $\operatorname{diag}D'\to\operatorname{diag}E$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. If $i:\operatorname{const}Y\to B$, $i':\operatorname{const}Z\to B'$ and $r:TY\to Z$ satisfy $bT(i)=i'\operatorname{const}(r)$, the maps from $H(S,Y)$, $H(TS,Z)$ and $H(S',Z)$ to the three diagonals induced by $i,i'$ form commuting squares with this span; the corresponding horizontal maps are $h\mapsto rT(h)$ and precomposition by $a$. Here $H(P,V)_m=\operatorname{Hom}(P^m,V)$.

source.place: Hovey, Model Categories, Theorem 5.2.8 (printed p.128), Proposition 5.4.7 (p.132), Lemma 5.5.1 (p.133); agent extraction of the Reedy lifting and comparison argument in the parent former step 12.

proof.text:
Use functional composition. For $\alpha:[k]\to[m]$ and $\beta:[l]\to[n]$, the operator on $D$ sends $h:S^m\to B_n$ to $B(\beta)hS(\alpha)$; use the same formula for $E,D'$, with $TS,B'$ and $S',B'$ respectively. Identity and composition laws follow from those of the diagrams, and the two directions commute by associativity. Naturality of $b$ gives
$$B'(\beta)b_nT(h)T(S(\alpha))=b_lT(B(\beta)hS(\alpha)).$$
Naturality of $a$ gives
$$B'(\beta)h'a^mT(S(\alpha))=B'(\beta)h'S'(\alpha)a^k.$$
Thus the two stated formulas commute with every pair of simplicial operators, so define the span $D\to E\leftarrow D'$ of bisimplicial sets. Restricting both indices along the diagonal gives the stated span of simplicial sets.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.7, bisimplicial Hom construction; the two naturality calculations are expanded here.

proof.text: Fix $m$ and put $X=TS^m$, $X'=S'^m$ and $f=a^m:X\to X'$. Both objects are cofibrant by hypothesis. Apply [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] to choose $X\xrightarrow{u}V\xrightarrow{p}X'$ and $s:X'\to V$, with $u,s$ cofibrations, $p$ a trivial fibration, $pu=f$ and $ps=1_{X'}$. Since $p,f$ and $1_{X'}$ are weak equivalences, two-out-of-three makes $u,s$ weak equivalences, hence trivial cofibrations. Write $J(A)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal N}(A,B'_n)$, with operators given by postcomposition with the operators of $B'$. Precomposition defines $J(v):J(C)\to J(A)$ for $v:A\to C$, and gives $J(wv)=J(v)J(w)$ and $J(1)=1$.

source.place: Lemma 1.1.12, explicit split factorization used in the Proposition 5.4.7 comparison.

proof.text: For either $v=u$ or $v=s$ from step 2, write $v:A\to C$. Consider a boundary lifting problem against $J(v):J(C)\to J(A)$ in dimension $n\geq0$. Its simplex on the lower side is a map $x:A\to B'_n$. Its upper boundary is a family $y_\theta:C\to B'_k$ for all proper injective $\theta:[k]\hookrightarrow[n]$, compatible with further face restrictions. These describe every boundary simplex: any nonsurjective order map into $[n]$ factors uniquely as a surjection onto its image followed by its proper injective image inclusion; the corresponding value is the degeneracy of $y_\theta$. The boundary relations are precisely the cone relations for $M_nB'$ in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], so the family gives $y:C\to M_nB'$. Commutativity of the original lifting problem says $q_nx=yv$, where $q_n:B'_n\to M_nB'$ is the matching map. Reedy fibrancy of $B'$ makes $q_n$ a fibration. Since $v$ is a trivial cofibration, the model-category lifting axiom supplies $z:C\to B'_n$ with $zv=x$ and $q_nz=y$. Its restrictions give a filler of the original boundary. For $n=0$ the boundary is empty and $M_0B'$ is terminal, so the same argument applies. Thus $J(u),J(s)$ have the right lifting property against every boundary and are trivial Kan fibrations by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper].

source.place: Proposition 5.4.1, dual boundary/matching calculation, and Corollary 5.4.4(2); here only trivial-cofibration lifting is needed.

proof.text: Step 3 makes $J(u),J(s)$ weak homotopy equivalences. The equation $ps=1_{X'}$ gives $J(s)J(p)=1_{J(X')}$. Two-out-of-three in the simplicial-set model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] therefore makes $J(p)$ a weak homotopy equivalence. From $f=pu$ obtain $J(f)=J(u)J(p)$, also a weak homotopy equivalence. For this fixed $m$, $J(f)$ is exactly $D'_{m,\bullet}\to E_{m,\bullet}$. This proves the required weak equivalence for every row. The Brown choices need not be natural in $m$: the map of bisimplicial sets was already defined independently in step 1.

source.place: Lemma 1.1.12, two-out-of-three argument; Proposition 5.4.7, row comparison.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence] to the actual bisimplicial map $D'\to E$ of step 1. Its hypothesis for every fixed first index is exactly step 4. It follows that $\operatorname{diag}D'\to\operatorname{diag}E$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. No cofibrancy of $S$ or Reedy cofibrancy of $TS,S'$ is used beyond the expressly assumed cofibrancy of the components of $a$ in step 2; neither a Quillen property of $T$ nor a weak-equivalence condition on $b$ is required.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.1, diagonal weak-equivalence argument used in Proposition 5.4.7.

proof.text:
The three vertical maps have degree-$m$ formulas
$$h\longmapsto i_mh,\qquad k\longmapsto i'_mk,\qquad h'\longmapsto i'_mh',$$
from $H(S,Y)$, $H(TS,Z)$, $H(S',Z)$ respectively to $\operatorname{diag}D$, $\operatorname{diag}E$, $\operatorname{diag}D'$. For example, for $\alpha:[k]\to[m]$, the first composite with its diagonal operator is $B(\alpha)i_mhS(\alpha)=i_khS(\alpha)$ by naturality of $i$; the other two calculations use naturality of $i'$. Thus these formulas define simplicial maps. The horizontal maps $h\mapsto rT(h)$ and $h'\mapsto h'a^m$ are simplicial by functoriality of $T$ and naturality of $a$, using the same computation as in step 1.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.7, maps from the constant-target mapping complexes; coaugmentation naturality written explicitly.

proof.text:
Check both squares on a degree-$m$ element. For $h:S^m\to Y$, the path via $D$ has value
$$b_mT(i_mh)=b_mT(i_m)T(h)=i'_mrT(h),$$
using exactly the assumed equation $bT(i)=i'\operatorname{const}(r)$. This is the path via $H(TS,Z)$. For $h':S'^m\to Z$, the path via $D'$ has value
$$(i'_mh')a^m=i'_m(h'a^m),$$
which is the path via $H(TS,Z)$. Equality in every degree gives equality of the simplicial maps of step 6, hence the two commuting squares with the span. These are strictly commuting squares; the statement asserts no weak equivalence for their vertical arrows under its present hypotheses.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.7 pattern; compatibility with the supplied coaugmentations is the displayed composition calculation.
